title: India clears $461 mn Kamarajar Port terminal
summary:
India's Cabinet panel has approved a PPP project for a second container terminal at Kamarajar Port, adding 2.0 million TEUs of annual capacity. 
The 900-metre terminal will be built under DBFOT in two phases at Rs 4,288.26 crore (~$461 million), with Rs 450 crore (~$48 million) dredging cost for KPL. 
It targets EXIM cargo from Chennai-Ennore and the southern hinterland.

title: French industrial producer price inflation accelerates to 9.6% in Oct
summary:
French industrial producer prices rose 1.5 per cent month on month in October 2026, while annual inflation accelerated to 9.6 per cent from 8.3 per cent in September, according to the INSEE. 
Higher energy costs drove the increase. 
Prices for products sold domestically rose 8.2 per cent year on year, while export prices increased 13.2 per cent. 
Import prices climbed 14.5 per cent annually.

title: Why is spandex down despite raw materials holding firm?
summary:
China's domestic spandex market ended the week softer, with every tracked denier below its November 18 level and 140D falling the most, down 1.84 per cent.
Finer grades held up better, with 20D down 0.63 per cent, 30D 0.65 per cent and 40D and 70D both 0.69 per cent.
PTMEG and BDO stayed steady to slightly firmer, squeezing producers as buyers waited for upstream costs to ease.

title: Nylon chips hold at $1.88/kg as raw material and demand ease
summary:
Nylon 6 chip prices in China stopped sliding this week, with HS chips closing at $1.883/kg on November 25, 0.69 per cent below the $1.896/kg level of November 17.
Upstream markets remain soft as caprolactam lost 1.02 per cent over the same period and benzene fell more than 5 per cent across Asian benchmarks.
The pause reflects producer resistance and margin repair, not yet a confirmed reversal.

title: North India cotton yarn prices steady amid weak demand
summary:
North India’s cotton yarn prices remained stable in Delhi and Ludhiana despite bearish sentiment from falling cotton, sluggish garment exports and subdued domestic demand.
Panipat recycled yarn held steady as limited textile waste supplies from Bangladesh offset weak demand and lower polyester fibre prices.
Cotton fell ₹70-80 (~$0.75-0.86) per maund as ICE futures weakened and arrivals reached 19,600 bales.

title: US tariff deal could give India’s T&A exporters competitive edge
summary:
India’s textile and apparel exporters could gain a US tariff edge if a trade deal with Washington succeeds.
USTR’s proposed additional tariff of up to 25 per cent could fall to 17 per cent under a reciprocal deal, replacing the current 10 per cent levy.
The gain could be 18 points over Vietnam, but just one point over Bangladesh, Cambodia and Indonesia; uncertainty may delay sourcing.

title: India’s economy kept its momentum in October, RBI officials say
summary:
India’s growth drivers and fundamentals remain buffers against geopolitical and supply risks, energy prices and financial uncertainty, the Reserve Bank of India bulletin said.
Momentum held in October on festive demand; Goods and Services Tax revenue hit its second-highest level since July 2017.
CPI inflation rose to 6.09 per cent; bank credit grew 19.5 per cent year on year at October-end.

title: Tüfekçi Makine to highlight textile climate control at India ITME 2026
summary:
Türkiye-based Tüfekçi Makine will participate in India ITME 2026 at Hall 11, Booth H11 F27, highlighting textile climate control, dust and fibre waste collection solutions.
Its systems focus on precise humidity management, balanced temperatures, controlled air distribution and energy efficiency to reduce yarn breakages, stabilise production and improve machinery performance.

title: China supplies 94% of India's polyester yarn imports: What's next?
summary:
India has extended its anti-dumping probe into Chinese polyester textured yarn until May 19, 2027, leaving sourcing risks unresolved.
TexPro says China supplied 94.05 per cent of India's PTY imports in 2025, as the PTY trade surplus fell to $99.22 million.
January-August 2026 PTY imports fell 2.84 per cent by volume while average value per tonne rose 19.48 per cent; India remains a net exporter.

title: Asia-Europe apparel freight faces $1,600 levy as delays persist
summary:
Asia-to-Mediterranean surcharges rise, led by CMA CGM’s $1,600 charge from November 25 and Maersk, Hapag-Lloyd and MSC tariffs.
Drewry’s global index fell 3 per cent, but Shanghai-Genoa and Far East-Mediterranean rates rose while some South Asian charges ease.
TexPro puts Asian apparel exports to selected European markets up 7.3 per cent; vessel delays threaten landed delivery dates.

title: US’ Nike revives Gyakusou running collection after five-year hiatus
summary:
Nike and Jun Takahashi are reviving Gyakusou with their first collection in more than five years, combining cold-weather running apparel with the Nike Alphafly 4 SP and Vomero Plus SP footwear.
The 2026 range launches December 3 through selected physical and Undercover channels, followed by a global release on December 11 via Nike, SNKRS and select retailers.

title: Bangladesh's RMG unrest persists as workers reject proposed $136 wage
summary:
Bangladesh’s garment industry remained disrupted as workers continued protests, highway blockades and factory attacks, rejecting the proposed monthly minimum wage of Tk17,000 (~$136), a 36 per cent increase from the existing rate. 
Demonstrations across Gazipur, Savar, Ashulia and Narayanganj highlighted workers’ dissatisfaction, with the proposed wage falling short of their demands.

title: Italy’s apparel imports drop 8.8% to $14.88 bn in Jan–Sept
summary:
Italy’s apparel imports fell 8.80 per cent YoY to $14.876 billion in January–September 2026 amid a broad sourcing slowdown.
China remained the top supplier at $2.719 billion, ahead of Spain and Bangladesh; all five leading suppliers posted declines.
Trousers and shorts led by product, while cotton and man-made fibre garments together made up nearly three-fourths of classified imports.

title: AAFA backs new US law to improve counterfeit detection & enforcement
summary:
AAFA has welcomed President Trump’s signing of the Customs Notification Act (H.R. 4930), saying it adds protection against illicit and dangerous goods ahead of peak holiday shopping. 
The law clarifies CBP information-sharing with brands during IP enforcement at the border, including data from products, packaging and packing materials. 
AAFA says it also expands who may receive CBP information.

title: Bangladesh's wage board proposes 36% hike to $136 for garment workers
summary:
Bangladesh's Minimum Wage Board has proposed a 36 per cent increase in the monthly minimum wage for garment workers to Tk17,000 ($136) from Tk12,500, following negotiations and a vote. 
The proposal awaits labour ministry approval, with implementation expected from December 2026. 
The decision follows weeks of worker protests demanding higher wages amid rising living costs.

title: US’ Nike extends Michigan State University partnership through 2035
summary:
Nike and Michigan State University have extended their all-sports partnership for eight years, carrying a 26-year relationship through June 30, 2035.
The deal includes custom basketball and football alternate uniforms, Michigan State-specific basketball footwear, Nike Sport Research Lab access for student-athletes and preferred Nike testing-partner recognition.

title: €58 mn denim shift raises stakes for Egypt, China and Bangladesh
summary:

Egypt gained $63.6 million, almost matching Bangladesh's $63.4 million loss, while China rose 20.23 per cent and Turkey lost $137.7 million.
TexPro trouser data and Egypt's garment network point to a 2027 contest over finishing and speed.

title: UK's Coats targets 2026 EBIT margin near 20% as profits stay resilient
summary:
UK's Coats expects full-year organic revenue to be broadly flat and earnings before interest and tax margin at or above 20 per cent, while strong free cash flow is set to reduce year-end leverage to around 2.0 times.
Revenue was flat organically in the four months to October 31, as apparel grew 3 per cent and footwear fell 7 per cent amid more pronounced destocking by brands.

title: Labour groups put living wage for Bangladesh garment workers at $265
summary:
Nine international labour rights organisations have urged Bangladesh’s RMG Minimum Wage Board to set wages in line with living costs during the ongoing review. 
They cited a living-wage estimate of about Tk 33,000 (~$265), alongside worker proposals of Tk 32,000 for skilled workers and Tk 30,000 for trainees. 
The groups also asked buyers to absorb increases and avoid shifting orders.

Students also toured KOTITI Testing & Research Institute to gain insights into textile quality, testing and research, supporting industry talent.
